claims.text: Because acknowledgment can precede application on secondaries, an immediate secondary read after a majority acknowledgment may not include that write. Use a causally consistent session with majority read and write concerns when the application needs to read its own acknowledged write from a secondary. (high confidence)

A May 2026 Reddit operator report describes a cache-refresh flow where a service read from a secondary after a majority-acknowledged write and could receive stale data; replies discuss primary reads and causal sessions. Treat this as an anecdotal impact report, not a measure of incidence. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-26)

Percona's February 4, 2025 comparison of Percona Server for MongoDB 8.0.4 and 7.0.15 across eight mongo-perf cases reported average gains of 12%, 7%, and 9% at 1, 4, and 8 threads. The comparison spans full releases and multiple operations, so it does not isolate the majority-ack change's contribution. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2025-02-04)

Starting in MongoDB 8.0, a { w: "majority" } replica-set write can be acknowledged once the calculated majority of data-bearing voting members durably writes the oplog entry; secondaries then apply the change asynchronously. Before 8.0, acknowledgment waited until the majority had applied the change. (high confidence)

MongoDB's current manual says the implicit default write concern is majority for most deployments, while MongoDB's 8.0 performance post says the default was w:1 before MongoDB 5.0. The 8.0 change is the acknowledgment point for majority writes, not the introduction of majority as the default. (high confidence)

With writeConcernMajorityJournalDefault set to true, MongoDB's default, { w: "majority" } acknowledgments wait for journal durability. If the setting is false, MongoDB can acknowledge before journal sync, and a transient loss or restart of a majority of replica-set members can roll back the write. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)

By removing secondary collection-apply time from the acknowledgment wait, the design aims to reduce primary latency and improve majority-write throughput. MongoDB's engineering account reports a significant prototype boost, and Alibaba Cloud describes improved throughput; neither makes a workload-independent speedup guarantee. (medium confidence)
